title: Watch Karol G & Bruno Mars Get Cozy & Playful Backstage in Sweet Video for ‘Still’
summary: The song is part of the Colombian star's latest album, No Me Arrepiento De Sentir Tanto.
contentText:
Karol G and Bruno Mars have really made the most out of their first-ever performance of their collaboration “Still.” On Wednesday (Sept. 2), the Colombian singer and the pop superstar released the music video for the song, filmed in the moments surrounding their Aug. 15 performance at the SoFi Stadium in Los Angeles that was part of her Viajando Por El Mundo Tropitour.

Mostly shot in black-and-white, the clip presents the two artists laughing in the seats, sharing a moment in the dressing room, riding a utility cart inside the venue and rehearsing on stage. It then bursts into color to showcase part of their live performance at a SoFi Stadium, in front of more than 50,000 fans, according to the press release.

“Still” is part of Karol G’s latest album, No Me Arrepiento de Sentir Tanto , which debuted at No. 1 on  Billboard ’s  Top Latin Albums  chart (dated Aug. 22) and at No. 8 on the all-genre  Billboard 200 .

A power ballad inspired by ’80s-fueled synthwave with a nostalgic, neon-soaked soundscape, the all-English track finds the Colombian artist and Mars harmonizing about unconditional love despite not being together anymore. “I still love you even with a broken heart,” they passionately croon.

In a video shared on TikTok on Aug. 7, Karol opened up about her collab with Mars.

“There’s a song on the album that’s entirely in English, and I don’t want people to just see it as, ‘Oh, Karol G’s new English song,’” she said. “I’ve always been open to making music in other languages — without pressure, as long as it flows and happens organically and naturally — and, well, that song found me. It expressed exactly what I was feeling and how I was feeling it; it was literally perfect for what I was going through, and I listened to it constantly. I tried to overthink it, but it was perfect — I hope it touches many people’s hearts.” 

Karol G’s North American stadium tour continues through Oct. 15, with stops in cities including Chicago, D.C. and Las Vegas before moving across Latin America and Europe, with more than 60 shows scheduled through July 2027. Meanwhile, Mars continues on his The Romantic Tour, which spans more than 115 stadium shows worldwide, following the release of his fourth solo album, The Romantic , which debuted at No. 1 on the Billboard 200.
